brief.headline: Jerónimo had a fall on 9/25 and new evening confusion since about mid-October. His grandson and sole caregiver Robert reported exhaustion on 11/22 and asked for respite.

items.statement: On 11/2 Robert reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, including once leaving the stove on. Jerónimo was oriented to person and place but not date, and had no fever. The plan was urinalysis, medication review and a PCP visit that week. The notes in this period show no results or follow-up for these, and the 11/13 nursing note says only 'no new concerns'.
items.verifier_note: The 11/2 note matches every detail: two weeks of evening confusion, the stove, orientation, no fever, and the plan. The 11/13 note says only 'No new concerns' and mentions no results or follow-up.

items.statement: Jerónimo fell at home on 9/25 getting out of bed. His grandson found him on the floor. He denied head strike or loss of consciousness and had a small left forearm skin tear, which was dressed. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed. No ED visit or hospital encounter is recorded in the period.
items.verifier_note: The 9/25 note matches all the clinical details. The encounters record is empty, so no ED or hospital visit is recorded.

items.statement: On 11/22 Robert, the primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed. This comes alongside the evening confusion and stove incident.
items.verifier_note: The 11/22 social work note matches the caregiver report, the respite request and what was discussed. The 11/2 note supports the link to the evening confusion and stove incident.

items.statement: The PT evaluation on 9/29 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, with PT twice weekly. Later notes do not document whether the walker, home evaluation or grab bars were put in place.
items.verifier_note: The PT evaluation matches on the gait findings, the TUG of 19 seconds, the recommendations and the twice-weekly frequency. The cited note does not document whether the equipment was put in place, so the statement's absence claim is consistent with it.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded for the current flu season, which started 8/1/2026.
items.verifier_note: The record shows flu_vaccine_this_season is false and the season began 8/1/2026. The only 2026 influenza dose is dated 6/30, before the season started.

questions_for_team: What were the results of the urinalysis and medication review ordered 11/2, and did the PCP visit happen?
Have the front-wheeled walker, home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars been completed, and how is PT progressing?
What evening supervision or respite can be arranged for Robert, and what stove safety measures are needed?
Does the team want a formal cognitive reassessment given the new evening confusion?
Should the flu vaccine be offered for this season?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in it: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, and observation stays, with discharge summaries and reasons.

Cardiac events: look for chest pain, nitroglycerin use, syncope, or new dyspnea in the window, given ischemic heart disease onset 2026-06-30 and new metoprolol, clopidogrel, nitroglycerin spray, and simvastatin starts on 2026-07-07. Check whether follow-up cardiology visits and any stress tests or procedures were completed or scheduled.

Heart rate and blood pressure trend since metoprolol start: resting HR, orthostatic BP, dizziness or light-headedness, and any reports of fatigue or bradycardia. Flag readings outside the team's agreed parameters for clinician review.

Bleeding risk review on clopidogrel: any bruising, melena, hematuria, epistaxis, or falls with head strike; check hemoglobin and platelet results if drawn. Also confirm whether any other antithrombotic or NSAID is on the record, since none is listed as active.
Lipid and statin check: confirm simvastatin adherence and whether a lipid panel and liver function tests were ordered after the statin start; note muscle symptoms reported.

Osteoporosis and fall-risk review: alendronic acid started 2026-06-30. Check adherence and administration instructions (fasting, upright positioning) being followed, any dysphagia or heartburn reports, any falls or fractures, and whether a DXA or calcium/vitamin D status is documented. Note the scoliosis history and any new back pain.

Falls screen across the window: number of falls, injuries, near-falls, and whether orthostatic symptoms from new beta-blocker or nitrate use are contributing. Check gait, assistive device use, and home safety notes.

Pain and migraine review: chronic pain and chronic intractable migraine. Count migraine days, rescue medication use, and any new or changed analgesics. Confirm no opioid or other controlled-substance changes were prescribed in the window, given the dependent drug abuse history (2018). Check prescription monitoring records and any mention of cravings, relapse, or withdrawal.

Substance use and mental health: review the dependent drug abuse history for any relapse signals, treatment engagement, and mood or anxiety screens (PHQ/GAD if available). Check attendance at any counseling or recovery services and any missed PACE day programme attendance.

Weight, nutrition, and dental: obesity (BMI 30+) with weight trend over the window; impacted molars history, so check for dental pain, extraction plans, or oral intake problems that could affect nutrition and medication swallowing. Also confirm care-plan items due: reassessment dates, caregiver check-in, and any outstanding referrals or consent updates.
